principle.name: Internal-Only Acceptance Criteria & Draft Precedence Override
principle.description: Acceptance criteria are strictly private internal checklists for Roo to evaluate fix correctness. They must never be included in GitHub issues or public artifacts. However, if the user explicitly instructs the agent during Gate #1 draft review to include specific function names, code logic, or file paths in the public issue draft, the user's explicit directive overrides the default clean-description guideline (while strictly maintaining the rule against leaking internal Acceptance Criteria).
principle.rationale: Keeps public issues clean for third parties while giving Roo precise validation criteria and honoring explicit user customization requests.

principle.name: Explicit Local Git Identity Scoping & Safe Command Batching
principle.description: Whenever setting fallback or temporary Git identity values, MUST ALWAYS use explicit scope flags (`git config --local user.name "..."`, `git config --local user.email "..."`). Furthermore, non-interactive sequential setup or Git operations may be batched within a single execution turn to save API round-trips, but arbitrary shell chaining operators (`&`, `;`, PowerShell `& { ... }`) are strictly banned. Command batching must NEVER cross any mandatory approval gate (Gate #1, Gate #2, Gate #3).
principle.rationale: Prevents global scope side-effects, syntax errors from shell operators, and premature gate bypassing.

principle.name: Gate #1 Universal Enforcement on Duplicate Overrides
principle.description: Selecting "Create new issue" after a duplicate search menu does NOT bypass Gate #1. The agent MUST always draft the public issue Markdown and halt execution at Hard Stop Gate #1 to present the draft and get explicit user confirmation before calling create_issue.
principle.rationale: Ensures human review of all issues even when overriding duplicate detection.

principle.name: Conditional Issue Assignment & Lazy Identity Resolution
principle.description: Resolve stakeholder identity lazily and only when an issue will remain open without an immediate automated fix (e.g., when the user declines an immediate fix). When retrieving local configuration, batch queries sequentially into as few turns as possible. If local identity info is unset, OR if the account search returns zero matching accounts, apply the unified fallback: assign the default repository owner if known, or prompt the user via `ask_followup_question` for the assignee handle. Never improvise alternate lookup strategies. Do not resolve identity or assign if the issue is being fixed immediately.
principle.rationale: Eliminates unnecessary API calls upfront and ensures consistent, predictable fallback behavior for both missing info and zero search matches.

principle.name: Exclusive Fix Delegation & No Direct File Editing
principle.description: The issue-management mode does not have file-editing permissions and must never perform file edits under any circumstances. All code modifications must be delegated to a dedicated implementation mode (Code or Orchestrator). There is no fallback to self-editing. Control returns to github-issue mode to review diffs and test results at Gate #3.
principle.rationale: Maintains strict separation of responsibilities between issue/PR orchestration and code implementation.

principle.name: Mandatory Duplicate Search Interception & Prompting
principle.description: Whenever search_issues returns a matching hit (open or closed), internal reasoning alone is insufficient—the agent MUST halt and explicitly prompt the user with choices (a) Link as related, (b) Comment on existing issue, or (c) Create new issue anyway before proceeding.
principle.rationale: Prevents duplicate issue creation and ensures user control over issue tracking.

principle.name: Mandatory User Confirmation Gates & Strict Turn Separation
principle.description: Always pause and ask the user before attempting a fix and before committing, pushing, or opening PRs (Hard Stop Gate #3). Furthermore, generating drafts or fix reviews and issuing tool calls must never happen in the same reasoning turn; the agent must halt and wait for explicit human response in a subsequent turn. Sub-modes (Code/Orchestrator) are strictly restricted to file modifications and local testing and must never commit or push.
principle.rationale: Ensures human-in-the-loop control over code modifications, verifies intent, and prevents implicit gate bypassing.

principle.name: PR Merge Attempt & Graceful Failure Handling (Phase 6)
principle.description: At the merge-decision point, always offer the user the choice to merge or leave the PR open for review without pre-evaluating permissions or claiming verified eligibility. If the user chooses to merge, attempt the merge directly via GitHub MCP. If the merge fails (permission error, branch protection, or failing checks), treat this as a normal expected outcome: report the actual error plainly, never claim success, do not retry automatically, and continue to workspace restoration (git checkout main && git pull).
principle.rationale: Avoids unsupportable pre-checks, prevents stuck retry loops, and guarantees accurate reporting to the user.

principle.name: Strict PR Lifecycle & Absolute Prohibition of Direct Pushes or Manual/Speculative Closures
principle.description: Bypassing Pull Request creation (e.g., pushing straight to main/master) and manually or speculatively closing issues via the Issues API (`update_issue`) are strictly prohibited under all circumstances. All fixes must be pushed to a regex-compliant feature branch (`issue-{number}-{short-slug}`), submitted via a rich Pull Request using `create_pull_request` with plain-text closing keywords (`Fixes #{number}`), and left open exclusively for automated GitHub webhook closure upon merge.
principle.rationale: Enforces traceability, audit trails, and automated GitHub lifecycle integration without speculative or premature state changes.

convention.rule: Branch names MUST strictly match the regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ (format: issue-{number}-{short-slug}). Bare issue numbers (e.g., issue-7), custom prefixes (e.g., fix-issue-5), and standard gitflow prefixes (e.g., fix/, feature/, bugfix/) are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN and will fail TC-4.3 evaluation checks.
Include plain-text issue references in commit titles, commit bodies, and PR descriptions. Never format references as Markdown links.

category.name: before_issue_creation
category.item: Parse repository origin URL from `git config --get remote.origin.url`
Check for duplicate open or closed issues using `search_issues` and explicitly prompt the user with choices (a, b, c) upon any matching hit
Verify acceptance criteria are excluded from public issue markdown (unless user explicitly overrides during Gate #1 draft review)

Get explicit user confirmation on the drafted issue Markdown BEFORE creating the issue on GitHub (Hard Stop Gate #1: strictly prohibited from calling `create_issue` in the same turn the draft is generated, even when overriding duplicate search results). If user requests custom description modifications, pause and wait for user's raw text input.

category.name: before_fixing
category.item: Ask user explicitly if we should attempt a fix (Hard Stop Gate #2)

If user declines fix, lazily resolve stakeholder identity by batching local config lookups and searching GitHub. If unset or no match found, apply unified fallback (default owner or prompt user), then assign the open issue.
If user approves fix, leave issue unassigned and delegate implementation to Code or Orchestrator mode (github-issue mode has no file editing capabilities).
Ensure fix is developed on a dedicated branch matching strict regex ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ (bare numbers and `fix/`/`feature/`/`bugfix/` prefixes are strictly forbidden)

category.name: before_pr_creation
category.item: Verify branch name matches exact regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$.
Ensure sub-mode (Code/Orchestrator) only modified files and ran tests without committing or pushing.
Get explicit user confirmation (Hard Stop Gate #3) on git diff and test output BEFORE executing git commit, git push, or creating the PR via `create_pull_request`.
Ensure commit and PR body use raw plain-text Fixes #{number} references (never bypass PR creation or push straight to main)
Verify NO manual issue closure API calls are made (`update_issue` state closure is strictly forbidden)

category.name: after_pr_creation
category.item: Offer the user the choice to merge the PR or leave it open for maintainer review without pre-evaluating permissions.
If user chooses to merge, attempt the merge directly. If the merge fails, report the error plainly, never claim false success, do not retry automatically, and proceed to workspace restoration.

Execute Phase 6 post-merge cleanup: return local workspace to main via git checkout main && git pull and delete feature branch upon successful merge (or keep remote branch intact if merge failed or was skipped).

Task completion is strictly invalid until Phase 6 is fully executed (merge offer/execution, local workspace restoration via git checkout main && git pull, and cleanup). Calling `attempt_completion` prematurely is strictly forbidden.
